# zig-ctap2 -- Complete API Reference

> Portable CTAP2/FIDO2 USB HID library in Zig with a stable C ABI for native applications on macOS and Linux.

Published documentation: https://transscendsurvival.org/zig-ctap2/. License: Zlib OR MIT.

## Installation

```bash
zig fetch --save git+https://github.com/Jesssullivan/zig-ctap2.git
```

Then in `build.zig`:

```zig
const dep = b.dependency("zig_ctap2", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
exe.root_module.addImport("zig-ctap2", dep.module("zig-ctap2"));
```

For C FFI consumers, build the static library and include `ctap2.h`:

```bash
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
```

Link `zig-out/lib/libctap2.a`. On macOS final applications also link `IOKit.framework` and `CoreFoundation.framework`; Linux uses hidraw and needs runtime access to `/dev/hidraw*`.

## Source Structure

- `src/root.zig` - Zig package API root
- `src/ffi.zig` - C FFI exports (16 functions)
- `src/cbor.zig` - Minimal CBOR encoder/decoder for the CTAP2 subset
- `src/ctap2.zig` - CTAP2 command encoding and response parsing
- `src/ctaphid.zig` - CTAPHID transport framing
- `src/pin.zig` - CTAP2 Client PIN protocol v2
- `src/hid.zig` - Platform-selected USB HID transport
- `src/hid_macos.zig` - macOS USB HID via IOKit
- `src/hid_linux.zig` - Linux USB HID via hidraw
- `include/ctap2.h` - C header
- `examples/` - C usage examples
- `tests/` - Unit, property-based, and hardware integration tests

## C API Reference

All functions are blocking with timeouts. Result data is written into caller-provided buffers. Return values use this convention: `0` is success for status-style functions, negative values are library errors, and positive values are CTAP2 device status bytes.

### Core Operations

- `ctap2_device_count()` - enumerate connected FIDO2 USB HID devices
- `ctap2_make_credential(...)` - perform authenticatorMakeCredential and return raw response bytes
- `ctap2_get_assertion(...)` - perform authenticatorGetAssertion and return raw response bytes
- `ctap2_get_info(...)` - perform authenticatorGetInfo and return raw response bytes

### Parsed Responses

- `ctap2_make_credential_parsed(...)` - makeCredential plus credential ID and attestation object parsing
- `ctap2_get_assertion_parsed(...)` - getAssertion plus credential ID, auth data, signature, and user handle parsing
- `ctap2_parse_make_credential_response(...)` - parse raw MakeCredential response without HID I/O
- `ctap2_parse_get_assertion_response(...)` - parse raw GetAssertion response without HID I/O

### PIN and Keepalive

- `ctap2_get_pin_retries(...)` - read remaining PIN retries
- `ctap2_get_pin_token(...)` - perform PIN protocol v2 token handshake
- `ctap2_make_credential_with_pin(...)` - PIN-authenticated registration
- `ctap2_get_assertion_with_pin(...)` - PIN-authenticated assertion
- `ctap2_make_credential_with_keepalive(...)` - registration with user-presence keepalive callback
- `ctap2_get_assertion_with_keepalive(...)` - assertion with user-presence keepalive callback

### Utilities

- `ctap2_status_message(status)` - map CTAP2 status byte to a static message string
- `ctap2_debug_last_ioreturn()` - return the last macOS IOKit return code, or `-1` on non-macOS platforms

## Build

```bash
zig build                        # static library
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast # optimized build
zig build test                   # unit tests
zig build test-pbt               # property-based tests
zig build test-hardware          # hardware tests; requires YUBIKEY_TESTS=1 and a device
zig build docs                   # Zig autodoc
zig build example                # C usage example build
```

## Apple / Swift / Objective-C Interop Scope

zig-ctap2 parallels only the USB HID CTAP2 portion of an Apple authenticator flow. It does not replace SwiftUI, AppKit, UIKit, Cocoa, AuthenticationServices UI, passkeys/iCloud Keychain, platform authenticators, browser WebAuthn policy, Secure Enclave, LocalAuthentication, biometric prompts, attestation policy validation, origin/RP policy, account sync, or application UI lifecycle.

Current gaps include SwiftPM/modulemap packaging, Objective-C nullability annotations, dedicated Swift wrapper types, WebAuthn request/response helpers, attestation validation, browser mediation semantics, Linux hidraw permission docs, NFC/BLE transport, and CTAP extensions such as hmac-secret/credProtect.
